newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Ministers fail to agree cereals penalty changes.
newsitem.headline: Ministers fail to agree cereals penalty changes.

text.p: European Union farm ministers failed on Monday to agree a proposal to make penalties for overplanting cereals and oilseeds more flexible, EU officials said.
"It was sent back for further study," said an official, adding the proposal was unlikely to resurface quickly.
A European Commission spokesman said that demands from six member states for even greater flexibility would weaken 1992 reforms to curb production surpluses.
The EU has just gathered in a record harvest and a halving of set-aside requirements to five percent would give an extra boost to 1997 production, the spokesman noted.
Germany, France and Italy, supported by Spain, Portugal and Greece want to target penalties on regions which exceeded planting limits but the Commission said this would make the system too complex.
Lack of agreement means that farmers are faced with national penalties and no special exemptions in countries, such as Spain, which are vulnerable to drought.
